title: Goal In One: 20 human-auditable level concepts (41-60)

coordinateSystem.boundingGeometry: outline from left floor to left wall and roof to right goal mouth; floor & goal segments synthesized via src/levels.ts segments()

currentTypes.Level: id, name, tip, par, starShots, width, start, goal, outline, obstacles, surfaces, movers, mechanics?, experimental?

physicsSnapshot.goalScore: ball crosses right-facing goal mouth at x goal.x + radius within vertical band

notSupportedDirectly: world-width/height dynamic bounds instead of fixed x=25,w=1250
independent collision full barriers with gates robustly animating into pocket
user-provided voice file for exactly one-shot goal
engineAudit.cameraNote: render.ts viewBounds currently uses fixed x=25 and width 1250, resize fits whole view; cameraX is exposed but not actually applied to camera transformation. New camera data requires code changes.
engineAudit.mobileNote: Render level in playable landscape viewport rather than scaling full scroll map. Compute world-to-screen and pointer-to-world using same camera offset. Mobile aiming hit area must exceed drawn 32-unit ball.
engineAudit.polygonNote: Vertices.clockwiseSort used in simulation.ts; design uses ONLY convex polygon obstacles; complex dividers decomposed into separate axis-aligned rectangles.
engineAudit.goalNote: segments(Level) joins outline last point to goal mouth and then goal roof/back, and floor from leftmost bottom point to net end. Never place a wall across the mouth.
engineAudit.mechanicNote: Switches use sensor circle radius 18, gates are stationary rectangle with animated position; physics QA MUST test that offset fully clears doorway and does not move into ball.
engineAudit.soundNote: audio.ts provides synthesized win jingle but not a real GOAL IN ONE spoken asset.

implementationContract.mustPreserve: Levels 1-40 unchanged. All new goals on right boundary. No mandatory shot limits. Mid-flight kicking and unlimited shots retained.
implementationContract.geometry: All level.outline points ordered left-bottom to roof -> mouth top; last point equals (goal.x, goal.y-goal.h). Each polygon convex. Gate bodies overlap surrounding partition by design; verify no corner leaks.
implementationContract.importStrategy: Create src/levels-41-60.generated.ts or JSON loader, parse canonical Level fields, add camera design metadata via type extension, append these levels without altering prior entries. Do not import design extras as physics objects.
implementationContract.cameraRules: fixed levels fit within safe content viewport; follow-x and follow-xy clamp camera rectangle to playable full world bounds (including goal net); add damping, dead zone, resize and pointer inversion.
implementationContract.physicsStatus: Concept only. Coordinate and schema checks are automated; zero actual kick trajectories tested in engine.

levels.name: Roof Ricochet
levels.tip: A deliberate bank shot off a level ceiling and angled backboard.

design.concept: A deliberate bank shot off a level ceiling and angled backboard.
design.reason: A central raised block defeats a lazy floor shot; the bankable roof and sloped return reward accurate power.
design.alternative: Two kicks over the block; short bounce off the wedge.
design.risk: Verify intended bank is achievable at default kick strength; do not advertise a guaranteed one-shot.
qa: Central block intercepts straight floor roll

levels.name: Window of Opportunity
levels.tip: Shoot through a mid-height gap between two solid dividers.

design.concept: Shoot through a mid-height gap between two solid dividers.
design.reason: A floor-to-roof divider removes all routes except a 112-unit-high midair window.
design.alternative: Use a careful second kick near the wedge to line up the window.
design.risk: Passage is only 112px high; ball diameter 32 means 80px effective clearance.

levels.name: Unlock the Passage
levels.tip: Hit the switch to open a compulsory gate through an otherwise sealed divider.

design.concept: Hit the switch to open a compulsory gate through an otherwise sealed divider.
design.reason: The divider spans roof to floor, so the switch-operated opening is the ONLY route toward the goal.
design.alternative: Try a single continuous ground kick that triggers the switch and then enters the opening.
design.risk: Confirm that the moving gate clears fully; gate travel must not squeeze the ball between wall colliders.
qa: Closed gate blocks every valid crossing

levels.name: Springboard
levels.tip: Use a spring to clear a wall, with a forgiving landing basin.

design.concept: Use a spring to clear a wall, with a forgiving landing basin.
design.reason: Spring is placed before a tall hurdle; an unaided direct roll cannot reach the goal.
design.alternative: A high direct kick followed by an airborne correction skips the spring.
design.risk: At default spring power, arc must clear the 145px hurdle without striking the low roof.

levels.name: Above or Below
levels.tip: Two distinct routes: a high platform shortcut or a narrow lower passage.

design.concept: Two distinct routes: a high platform shortcut or a narrow lower passage.
design.reason: The overhead bridge avoids the lower solid stop; both routes stay within the enclosed arena.
design.alternative: Stay underneath and steer through the lower route with extra shots.
design.risk: Ensure 34px bridge thickness is visually clear and upper route has clearance.

levels.name: Crosswind Slot
levels.tip: Ride an updraft through a safe opening, then correct the descent.

design.concept: Ride an updraft through a safe opening, then correct the descent.
design.reason: Wind supplies lift exactly where the floor obstacle begins; overhead fin makes air control important.
design.alternative: Skip the updraft with multiple manual midair kicks.
design.risk: Airflow should be readable, not violently unpredictable.

levels.name: Break or Bypass
levels.tip: Smash the breakable shortcut, or take an elevated detour.

design.concept: Smash the breakable shortcut, or take an elevated detour.
design.reason: The fragile block closes the most direct route, while a loft path remains above it.
design.alternative: Launch from the ramp onto the higher rail and bypass the breakable.
design.risk: Damage must be achievable at default shot speeds; breakables are not intended to be unbreakable walls.

levels.name: Clockwork Gap
levels.tip: Wait for a slow rotor to offer an opening, or use it to redirect the ball.

design.concept: Wait for a slow rotor to offer an opening, or use it to redirect the ball.
design.reason: Rotating blade dominates the central travel corridor and changes the shot timing.
design.alternative: Roll low beneath a favourable rotor orientation after a setup kick.
design.risk: Rotor collision updates must not tunnel or trap the football.

levels.name: Ice Corridor
levels.tip: Preserve sliding speed across ice then handle a sharp rise.

design.concept: Preserve sliding speed across ice then handle a sharp rise.
design.reason: A long low-friction runway encourages speed control before a final incline.
design.alternative: Short repeated kicks or intentional wall bank.
design.risk: Verify that the low-friction body does not inherit unintended regular-floor friction.

levels.name: The Timed Door
levels.tip: Activate a switch, then reach a compulsory lower gate before it closes.

design.concept: Activate a switch, then reach a compulsory lower gate before it closes.
design.reason: The closing gate is essential because the upper partition physically blocks the entire rest of the height.
design.alternative: A fast single shot could trigger the timed switch and clear the gate before re-closing.
design.risk: Test switch activation window plus gate travel; 8 seconds must be sufficient for ordinary multi-kick players.

levels.name: High Switch
levels.tip: Trigger an elevated switch to unblock the low ground route.

design.concept: Trigger an elevated switch to unblock the low ground route.
design.reason: Only the gate-side gap connects left and right. An elevated target adds a meaningful preliminary objective.
design.alternative: A wall bank can activate the switch in one shot, followed by a low finish.
design.risk: If the upper switch is too high for one kick, reduce its position rather than requiring frame-perfect aim.

levels.name: The Z-Corridor
levels.tip: Use staggered upper and lower blocks to thread a non-linear path.

design.concept: Use staggered upper and lower blocks to thread a non-linear path.
design.reason: Staggered floor-to-near-roof blockers remove direct line-of-sight; each kick solves a distinct segment.
design.alternative: One-shot double bank for expert players, if physics makes it possible.
design.risk: Keep generous gaps around baffle tips: minimum 95px after subtracting ball diameter.

levels.name: Longshot Relay
levels.tip: A rolling course with separated spring and rotor stages.

design.concept: A rolling course with separated spring and rotor stages.
design.reason: Spring is placed just before a tall wall; the rotor then presents a qualitatively different timing challenge.
design.alternative: Careful kicks can clear each stage without relying entirely on the mechanics.
design.risk: Do not zoom out to show the entire 2,245px world; demonstrate live horizontal camera following.

levels.name: Updraft Shaft
levels.tip: Climb vertically through an upper doorway, then descend into the goal chamber.

design.concept: Climb vertically through an upper doorway, then descend into the goal chamber.
design.reason: Full-height divider is traversable only via an elevated window. The wind makes the upper section reachable.
design.alternative: Manual midair kicks or spring-like rebounds could reach the window if strong enough.
design.risk: Requires vertical camera tracking and precise view of switch-free high pass; passage 95px tall (63px effective).

levels.name: Three Chambers
levels.tip: Cross two sealed room dividers by activating a switch in each preceding chamber.

design.concept: Cross two sealed room dividers by activating a switch in each preceding chamber.
design.reason: Two floor-to-ceiling structural partitions provide two genuinely required gated corridors; second switch is past gate one.
design.alternative: After opening gates, a skilled player may use long rolling shots through each section.
design.risk: Both switches must only control their intended gates; check clipping at closed-door seams.

levels.name: Hazard Overpass
levels.tip: Reach an elevated safe route above a long series of red resets.

design.concept: Reach an elevated safe route above a long series of red resets.
design.reason: Hazard makes pure floor traversal costly; elevated bridge gives a readable safe sequence.
design.alternative: Long aerial shots across the hazard using multiple midair corrections.
design.risk: Delete surface must allow 1-shot attempts without accidental unavoidable respawn on the far side.

levels.name: Wind and Workshop
levels.tip: A wind-assisted passage ending at a mandatory switch-operated door.

design.concept: A wind-assisted passage ending at a mandatory switch-operated door.
design.reason: Upward wind changes how to negotiate the raised shelf, but a mandatory gate still controls the last chamber.
design.alternative: Multi-kick low bypass of some wind effects before compulsory switch.
design.risk: Wind should not throw the ball outside camera view; timing gate remains generous.

levels.name: Skybridge Return
levels.tip: Rise to the upper bridge; use a narrow midheight doorway to cross.

design.concept: Rise to the upper bridge; use a narrow midheight doorway to cross.
design.reason: Midheight doorway is the only route past a full-height divider, forcing a genuinely multi-area ascent.
design.alternative: Skilled aerial kicks can bypass the auxiliary wind after reaching bridge height.
design.risk: Camera must follow vertical movement without hiding destination platform; safe reset after hazard.

levels.name: Switchback Factory
levels.tip: Two meaningful gated partitions and a slippery transition between them.

design.concept: Two meaningful gated partitions and a slippery transition between them.
design.reason: A second gate physically separates the last room, and the ice creates a distinct momentum-control segment.
design.alternative: Time long ground kicks so the ball triggers one switch while already moving towards its gate.
design.risk: Ice must not send ball into the second closed gate so fast that rebounds appear unpredictable.

levels.name: The Grand Route
levels.tip: Five concise puzzle beats: spring, airflow, a breakable shortcut, compulsory gate and finishing rotor.

design.concept: Five concise puzzle beats: spring, airflow, a breakable shortcut, compulsory gate and finishing rotor.
design.reason: Each beat changes the player decision; the final door is compulsory, while spring/wind/wood/rotor allow skillful alternatives.
design.alternative: Expert multi-kick route can skip the spring and breakable but never bypass the final physical gate.
design.risk: This is an exploratory finale, not a fixed automatic chain; verify camera readability and softlock avoidance section-by-section.
